catolicos_1952.subtitle: Catholic population, by province, 1952, persons
catolicos_1952.definition: Persons declaring the Catholic religion in the 1952 population census, by province, from Censo 1952, Tomo 1 (Resumen del País), Servicio Nacional de Estadística y Censos. Religion was self-declared by respondents. A single-year cross-section; protestantes_1952 and sin_religion_1952 carry the remaining declared categories.

protestantes_1952.subtitle: Protestant and Evangelical population, by province, 1952, persons
protestantes_1952.definition: Persons declaring a Protestant or Evangelical religion in the 1952 population census, by province, from Censo 1952, Tomo 1 (Resumen del País), Servicio Nacional de Estadística y Censos. Religion was self-declared by respondents. A single-year cross-section; the companion indicators are catolicos_1952 and sin_religion_1952.

sin_religion_1952.subtitle: Population declaring no religion, by province, 1952, persons
sin_religion_1952.definition: Persons declaring no religion in the 1952 population census, by province, from Censo 1952, Tomo 1 (Resumen del País), Servicio Nacional de Estadística y Censos. Religion was self-declared, so the category mixes irreligion with refusal to name a denomination. A single-year cross-section.

chilenos_total_1952.subtitle: Chilean-born population, by province, 1952, persons
chilenos_total_1952.definition: Population of Chilean nationality counted in the 1952 census, by province, from Censo 1952, Tomo 1 (Resumen del País), Servicio Nacional de Estadística y Censos. The complement of extranjeros_total_1952 within the census total. A single-year cross-section.

extranjeros_total_1952.subtitle: Foreign-born population, by province, 1952, persons
extranjeros_total_1952.definition: Foreign nationals counted in the 1952 population census, by province, from Censo 1952, Tomo 1 (Resumen del País), Servicio Nacional de Estadística y Censos. Continues the foreigner counts the 19th-century censuses reported by department. A single-year cross-section.

superficie_km2_1952.subtitle: Territorial area, by province, 1952, square kilometers
superficie_km2_1952.definition: Territorial extent of each province in square kilometers as printed in Censo 1952, Tomo 1 (Resumen del País), Servicio Nacional de Estadística y Censos. Reflects the administrative boundaries in force at the 1952 census and serves as the denominator of densidad_1952. A single-year cross-section.

densidad_1952.subtitle: Population density, by province, 1952, persons per km²
densidad_1952.definition: Population per square kilometer at the 1952 census, by province, as printed in Censo 1952, Tomo 1 (Resumen del País), Servicio Nacional de Estadística y Censos: the ratio of the census population to the provincial area (superficie_km2_1952). A single-year cross-section.

casados_1952.subtitle: Married population aged 15 and over, by province, 1952, persons
casados_1952.definition: Persons aged 15 and over declaring themselves married at the 1952 census, by province, from the civil-status table of Censo 1952, Tomo 1 (Resumen del País), Servicio Nacional de Estadística y Censos. A single-year cross-section; solteros_1952 and viudos_1952 carry the other civil-status categories.

solteros_1952.subtitle: Single population aged 15 and over, by province, 1952, persons
solteros_1952.definition: Persons aged 15 and over declaring themselves single at the 1952 census, by province, from the civil-status table of Censo 1952, Tomo 1 (Resumen del País), Servicio Nacional de Estadística y Censos. A single-year cross-section; casados_1952 and viudos_1952 carry the other civil-status categories.

viudos_1952.subtitle: Widowed population aged 15 and over, by province, 1952, persons
viudos_1952.definition: Persons aged 15 and over declaring themselves widowed at the 1952 census, by province, from the civil-status table of Censo 1952, Tomo 1 (Resumen del País), Servicio Nacional de Estadística y Censos. A single-year cross-section; casados_1952 and solteros_1952 carry the other civil-status categories.

poblacion_activa_1952.subtitle: Economically active population, by province, 1952, persons
poblacion_activa_1952.definition: Economically active population at the 1952 census, by province, from Censo 1952, Tomo 1 (Resumen del País), Servicio Nacional de Estadística y Censos: persons who declared an occupation or were seeking work, under the census definition of the labor force. A single-year cross-section.

con_instruccion_primaria_1952.subtitle: Population with primary schooling, by province, 1952, persons
con_instruccion_primaria_1952.definition: Persons reporting primary school as their level of instruction at the 1952 census, by province, from Censo 1952, Tomo 1 (Resumen del País), Servicio Nacional de Estadística y Censos. Measures attainment declared to enumerators, not enrollment. A single-year cross-section; secondary and university attainment are separate indicators.

con_instruccion_secundaria_1952.subtitle: Population with secondary schooling, by province, 1952, persons
con_instruccion_secundaria_1952.definition: Persons reporting secondary school as their level of instruction at the 1952 census, by province, from Censo 1952, Tomo 1 (Resumen del País), Servicio Nacional de Estadística y Censos. Measures attainment declared to enumerators, not enrollment. A single-year cross-section.

con_instruccion_universitaria_1952.subtitle: Population with university education, by province, 1952, persons
con_instruccion_universitaria_1952.definition: Persons reporting university-level instruction at the 1952 census, by province, from Censo 1952, Tomo 1 (Resumen del País), Servicio Nacional de Estadística y Censos. Measures attainment declared to enumerators, not enrollment. A single-year cross-section.

poblacion_hombres_1970.subtitle: Male population, by comuna, 1970, persons
poblacion_hombres_1970.definition: Male population counted by comuna at the 1970 population census. Extracted from the CIREN folletos Características Básicas de la Población; the printed hombres + mujeres = total identity holds for every comuna. Coverage follows the folleto set processed to date, so a few comunas are absent.

poblacion_mujeres_1970.subtitle: Female population, by comuna, 1970, persons
poblacion_mujeres_1970.definition: Female population counted by comuna at the 1970 population census. Extracted from the CIREN folletos Características Básicas de la Población; the printed hombres + mujeres = total identity holds for every comuna. Coverage follows the folleto set processed to date, so a few comunas are absent.

poblacion_urbana_1970.subtitle: Urban population, by comuna, 1970, persons
poblacion_urbana_1970.definition: Population living in localities classified as urban by the 1970 census, by comuna. Extracted from the CIREN folletos Características Básicas de la Población; the printed hombres + mujeres = total identity holds for every comuna. Coverage follows the folleto set processed to date, so a few comunas are absent.

poblacion_rural_1970.subtitle: Rural population, by comuna, 1970, persons
poblacion_rural_1970.definition: Population living outside localities classified as urban by the 1970 census, by comuna. Extracted from the CIREN folletos Características Básicas de la Población; the printed hombres + mujeres = total identity holds for every comuna. Coverage follows the folleto set processed to date, so a few comunas are absent.

poblacion_urbana_hombres_1970.subtitle: Urban male population, by comuna, 1970, persons
poblacion_urbana_hombres_1970.definition: Male population living in localities classified as urban by the 1970 census, by comuna. Extracted from the CIREN folletos Características Básicas de la Población; the printed hombres + mujeres = total identity holds for every comuna. Coverage follows the folleto set processed to date, so a few comunas are absent.

poblacion_urbana_mujeres_1970.subtitle: Urban female population, by comuna, 1970, persons
poblacion_urbana_mujeres_1970.definition: Female population living in localities classified as urban by the 1970 census, by comuna. Extracted from the CIREN folletos Características Básicas de la Población; the printed hombres + mujeres = total identity holds for every comuna. Coverage follows the folleto set processed to date, so a few comunas are absent.

poblacion_rural_hombres_1970.subtitle: Rural male population, by comuna, 1970, persons
poblacion_rural_hombres_1970.definition: Male population living outside localities classified as urban by the 1970 census, by comuna. Extracted from the CIREN folletos Características Básicas de la Población; the printed hombres + mujeres = total identity holds for every comuna. Coverage follows the folleto set processed to date, so a few comunas are absent.

poblacion_rural_mujeres_1970.subtitle: Rural female population, by comuna, 1970, persons
poblacion_rural_mujeres_1970.definition: Female population living outside localities classified as urban by the 1970 census, by comuna. Extracted from the CIREN folletos Características Básicas de la Población; the printed hombres + mujeres = total identity holds for every comuna. Coverage follows the folleto set processed to date, so a few comunas are absent.

poblacion_hombres_1992.subtitle: Male population, by comuna, 1992, persons
poblacion_hombres_1992.definition: Male population counted by comuna at the 1992 population and housing census, from the born-digital INE census volume (Cuadro 1). Comuna totals reconcile to the national census population. A single-year cross-section.

poblacion_mujeres_1992.subtitle: Female population, by comuna, 1992, persons
poblacion_mujeres_1992.definition: Female population counted by comuna at the 1992 population and housing census, from the born-digital INE census volume (Cuadro 1). Comuna totals reconcile to the national census population. A single-year cross-section.

viviendas_particulares_1992.subtitle: Private dwellings, by comuna, 1992, dwellings
viviendas_particulares_1992.definition: Private (household) dwellings counted by comuna in the 1992 population and housing census (INE, volume Ciudades, Pueblos y Aldeas). Excludes collective dwellings such as hospitals, barracks, and convents, carried in viviendas_colectivas_1992.

viviendas_colectivas_1992.subtitle: Collective dwellings, by comuna, 1992, dwellings
viviendas_colectivas_1992.definition: Collective dwellings, such as hospitals, barracks, convents, hotels, and other institutional quarters, counted by comuna in the 1992 population and housing census (INE, volume Ciudades, Pueblos y Aldeas). The complement of viviendas_particulares_1992 within total dwellings.

viviendas_permanentes_1992.subtitle: Permanent dwellings, by comuna, 1992, dwellings
viviendas_permanentes_1992.definition: Dwellings of permanent construction (houses and apartments) as classified by the census, counted by comuna in the 1992 population and housing census (INE, volume Ciudades, Pueblos y Aldeas). Semi-permanent and mobile structures are carried in the companion indicators.

viviendas_semipermanentes_1992.subtitle: Semi-permanent dwellings, by comuna, 1992, dwellings
viviendas_semipermanentes_1992.definition: Dwellings of semi-permanent construction, such as mejoras and mediaguas, as classified by the census, counted by comuna in the 1992 population and housing census (INE, volume Ciudades, Pueblos y Aldeas). An indicator of precarious housing stock.

viviendas_moviles_otros_1992.subtitle: Mobile and other dwellings, by comuna, 1992, dwellings
viviendas_moviles_otros_1992.definition: Mobile dwellings (tents, wagons, boats) and other structures not classifiable as permanent or semi-permanent, counted by comuna in the 1992 population and housing census (INE, volume Ciudades, Pueblos y Aldeas). The residual dwelling-type category; counts are small in most comunas.

viviendas_tenencia_arrendada_1992.subtitle: Rented dwellings, by comuna, 1992, dwellings
viviendas_tenencia_arrendada_1992.definition: Occupied dwellings whose households declared rented tenure, counted by comuna in the 1992 population and housing census (INE, volume Ciudades, Pueblos y Aldeas). Owner-occupied and other tenure forms are carried in the companion tenure indicators.

viviendas_tenencia_otra_1992.subtitle: Dwellings under other tenure, by comuna, 1992, dwellings
viviendas_tenencia_otra_1992.definition: Occupied dwellings under tenure other than ownership or rental, such as ceded, employer-provided, or usufruct arrangements, counted by comuna in the 1992 population and housing census (INE, volume Ciudades, Pueblos y Aldeas).

viviendas_agua_con_caneria_1992.subtitle: Dwellings with piped water, by comuna, 1992, dwellings
viviendas_agua_con_caneria_1992.definition: Dwellings with piped water inside the dwelling, counted by comuna in the 1992 population and housing census (INE, volume Ciudades, Pueblos y Aldeas). A basic-services indicator; the complement is split between viviendas_agua_sin_caneria_1992 and viviendas_agua_otra_fuente_1992.

viviendas_agua_sin_caneria_1992.subtitle: Dwellings without piped water, by comuna, 1992, dwellings
viviendas_agua_sin_caneria_1992.definition: Dwellings whose water supply is not piped into the dwelling, counted by comuna in the 1992 population and housing census (INE, volume Ciudades, Pueblos y Aldeas). A basic-services deficit indicator.

viviendas_agua_otra_fuente_1992.subtitle: Dwellings using another water source, by comuna, 1992, dwellings
viviendas_agua_otra_fuente_1992.definition: Dwellings drawing water from sources other than a piped network, such as wells, rivers, or water trucks, counted by comuna in the 1992 population and housing census (INE, volume Ciudades, Pueblos y Aldeas). Concentrated in rural comunas.

viviendas_sin_alumbrado_electrico_1992.subtitle: Dwellings without electric lighting, by comuna, 1992, dwellings
viviendas_sin_alumbrado_electrico_1992.definition: Dwellings without electric lighting, counted by comuna in the 1992 population and housing census (INE, volume Ciudades, Pueblos y Aldeas). A basic-services deficit indicator; by 1992 counts are small outside rural comunas.

viviendas_sin_alcantarillado_1992.subtitle: Dwellings without sewerage, by comuna, 1992, dwellings
viviendas_sin_alcantarillado_1992.definition: Dwellings without connection to a sewerage system, counted by comuna in the 1992 population and housing census (INE, volume Ciudades, Pueblos y Aldeas). A basic-services deficit indicator, higher in rural and peri-urban comunas.

poblacion_media_1928.subtitle: Estimated mid-year population, by department and province, 1928, persons
poblacion_media_1928.definition: Estimated mid-year (media) population for 1928, by department and province, from the Anuario Estadístico de Chile 1928 (Dirección General de Estadística). An administrative intercensal estimate between the 1920 and 1930 censuses, not a census enumeration. A single-year cross-section.

ruralpop_pct.subtitle: Rural population share, by comuna, 1935, %
ruralpop_pct.definition: Share of the comuna population classified as rural, in %, in the 1935 commune frame, from the curated research assembly regime-state 1935.xlsx, the author's compilation of official mid-1930s comuna statistics. The assembly carries no page-level citation, so the series documents a compilation rather than a direct extraction. A single-year cross-section used as a control in the regime-state analyses.

revenue_customs_pesos.subtitle: Customs revenue, national, 1846–1888, nominal pesos
revenue_customs_pesos.definition: Ordinary fiscal revenue collected by the customs houses (aduanas), in nominal pesos, 1846-1888. The dominant single source of state revenue throughout the period. Compiled from the ramo-level receipts printed in the Anuario Estadístico de Chile 1860 and the Memorias del Ministerio de Hacienda; category totals are sums of the primary ramos as printed, with each cell citing its source volume.
revenue_customs_pesos.units_note: Nominal pesos of the day; no deflation applied across the series.

revenue_direct_taxes_pesos.subtitle: Direct tax revenue, national, 1846–1888, nominal pesos
revenue_direct_taxes_pesos.definition: Ordinary fiscal revenue from direct contributions, chiefly the agricultural land tax (catastro) and related levies on property and income, in nominal pesos, 1846-1888. Compiled from the ramo-level receipts printed in the Anuario Estadístico de Chile 1860 and the Memorias del Ministerio de Hacienda; category totals are sums of the primary ramos as printed, with each cell citing its source volume.
revenue_direct_taxes_pesos.units_note: Nominal pesos of the day; no deflation applied across the series.

revenue_indirect_taxes_pesos.subtitle: Indirect and internal tax revenue, national, 1846–1888, nominal pesos
revenue_indirect_taxes_pesos.definition: Ordinary fiscal revenue from internal indirect taxation, including the alcabala transfer tax, stamped paper, and commercial patentes (assigned to this category by convention), in nominal pesos, 1846-1888. Compiled from the ramo-level receipts printed in the Anuario Estadístico de Chile 1860 and the Memorias del Ministerio de Hacienda; category totals are sums of the primary ramos as printed, with each cell citing its source volume.
revenue_indirect_taxes_pesos.units_note: Nominal pesos of the day; no deflation applied across the series.

revenue_mining_taxes_pesos.subtitle: Mining tax revenue, national, 1846–1888, nominal pesos
revenue_mining_taxes_pesos.definition: Ordinary fiscal revenue from levies specific to mining, in nominal pesos, 1846-1888. Recorded as zero before the nitrate era by construction, since pre-nitrate mining receipts flowed through other ramos. Compiled from the ramo-level receipts printed in the Anuario Estadístico de Chile 1860 and the Memorias del Ministerio de Hacienda; category totals are sums of the primary ramos as printed, with each cell citing its source volume.
revenue_mining_taxes_pesos.units_note: Nominal pesos of the day; no deflation applied across the series.

revenue_other_taxes_pesos.subtitle: Other ordinary revenue, national, 1846–1888, nominal pesos
revenue_other_taxes_pesos.definition: Residual ordinary fiscal revenue outside the customs, direct, indirect, and mining categories, in nominal pesos, 1846-1888; before 1853 it includes the diezmo (tithe) receipts, assigned here by convention. Compiled from the ramo-level receipts printed in the Anuario Estadístico de Chile 1860 and the Memorias del Ministerio de Hacienda; category totals are sums of the primary ramos as printed, with each cell citing its source volume.
revenue_other_taxes_pesos.units_note: Nominal pesos of the day; no deflation applied across the series.

revenue_total_ordinary_pesos.subtitle: Total ordinary fiscal revenue, national, 1846–1888, nominal pesos
revenue_total_ordinary_pesos.definition: Total ordinary fiscal revenue of the central state, in nominal pesos, 1846-1888: the sum of the customs, direct, indirect, mining, and other categories. Compiled from the ramo-level receipts printed in the Anuario Estadístico de Chile 1860 and the Memorias del Ministerio de Hacienda; category totals are sums of the primary ramos as printed, with each cell citing its source volume.
revenue_total_ordinary_pesos.units_note: Nominal pesos of the day; no deflation applied across the series.

valor_minero_total_1914.subtitle: Mining production value, by province, 1914, pesos
valor_minero_total_1914.definition: Total declared value of mining and metallurgical production by province in 1914, in nominal pesos, from the Anuario Estadístico de Chile 1914, Vol. VII (Minería y Metalurgia). A single-year cross-section dominated by the nitrate provinces of the north.

salitre_production_tons.subtitle: Nitrate (salitre) production, national, 1880–1927, metric tons
salitre_production_tons.definition: Annual national production of nitrate (salitre) in metric tons, 1880-1927, from the retrospective series of the Sinopsis Estadística de Chile 1900 and 1924-27. Nitrate was the export backbone of the post-War of the Pacific economy and the base of the export tax that dominated fiscal revenue until the synthetic-nitrate collapse.

escuelas_publicas_primarias_1913.subtitle: Public primary schools, by province, 1913, schools
escuelas_publicas_primarias_1913.definition: Number of public primary schools in operation by province in 1913, from the Anuario Estadístico de Chile 1913, Vol. V (Instrucción). Private schools are excluded. A single-year cross-section; escuelas_1914 carries the following year.

escuelas_1914.subtitle: Public primary schools, by province, 1914, schools
escuelas_1914.definition: Number of public primary schools in operation by province in 1914, from the Anuario Estadístico de Chile 1914, Vol. V (Instrucción). Private schools are excluded. A single-year cross-section; the companion enrollment and attendance indicators are matricula_total_1914 and asistencia_media_total_1914.

matricula_total_1914.subtitle: Primary school enrollment, by province, 1914, pupils
matricula_total_1914.definition: Pupils enrolled (matrícula) in public primary schools by province in 1914, from the Anuario Estadístico de Chile 1914, Vol. V (Instrucción). Enrollment overstates effective schooling; average attendance (asistencia_media_total_1914) is the stricter measure. A single-year cross-section.

asistencia_media_total_1914.subtitle: Average primary school attendance, by province, 1914, pupils
asistencia_media_total_1914.definition: Average daily attendance (asistencia media) in public primary schools by province in 1914, from the Anuario Estadístico de Chile 1914, Vol. V (Instrucción). The stricter measure of effective schooling, typically well below enrollment (matricula_total_1914). A single-year cross-section.

pres_int_n_posts.subtitle: Budgeted administrative posts, Interior, by province and department, 1890–1896, posts
pres_int_n_posts.definition: Number of budgeted posts (plazas) in the territorial administration, from the annual Lei de Presupuestos of the Ministerio del Interior, 1890-1896. These are authorized appropriations for the territorial administration (intendencias and gobernaciones), not executed spending.

pres_int_sueldos_pesos.subtitle: Budgeted salaries, Interior, by province and department, 1890–1896, nominal pesos
pres_int_sueldos_pesos.definition: Salary appropriations (sueldos fijos) in nominal pesos for the territorial administration, from the annual Lei de Presupuestos of the Ministerio del Interior, 1890-1896. These are authorized appropriations for the territorial administration (intendencias and gobernaciones), not executed spending.

pres_int_operativos_pesos.subtitle: Budgeted operating expenses, Interior, by province and department, 1890–1896, nominal pesos
pres_int_operativos_pesos.definition: Operating-expense appropriations (gastos variables) in nominal pesos for the territorial administration, from the annual Lei de Presupuestos of the Ministerio del Interior, 1890-1896. These are authorized appropriations for the territorial administration (intendencias and gobernaciones), not executed spending.

income.subtitle: Municipal income, by comuna, 1935, nominal pesos
income.definition: Total municipal revenue by comuna, in nominal pesos, for 1935, from the curated research assembly regime-state 1935.xlsx, the author's compilation of official mid-1930s comuna statistics. The assembly carries no page-level citation, so the series documents a compilation rather than a direct extraction. A single-year cross-section; taxincome and salaries carry the tax-revenue and salary-spending components.

taxincome.subtitle: Municipal tax income, by comuna, 1935, nominal pesos
taxincome.definition: Municipal revenue raised through local taxation by comuna, in nominal pesos, for 1935, from the curated research assembly regime-state 1935.xlsx, the author's compilation of official mid-1930s comuna statistics. The assembly carries no page-level citation, so the series documents a compilation rather than a direct extraction. A component of income; the ratio of the two measures local fiscal effort.

salaries.subtitle: Municipal salary spending, by comuna, 1935, nominal pesos
salaries.definition: Municipal spending on salaries by comuna, in nominal pesos, for 1935, from the curated research assembly regime-state 1935.xlsx, the author's compilation of official mid-1930s comuna statistics. The assembly carries no page-level citation, so the series documents a compilation rather than a direct extraction. A single-year cross-section.

pubadm.subtitle: Public administration spending, by comuna, 1935, nominal pesos
pubadm.definition: Spending on public administration by comuna, in nominal pesos, for 1935, from the curated research assembly regime-state 1935.xlsx, the author's compilation of official mid-1930s comuna statistics. The assembly carries no page-level citation, so the series documents a compilation rather than a direct extraction. A proxy for the local presence of the state. A single-year cross-section.
pubadm.units_note: The assembly codebook carries no unit statement; nominal pesos inferred from magnitudes consistent with the municipal budget columns.

police1920.subtitle: Police personnel, by comuna, 1920, persons
police1920.definition: Police personnel stationed in the comuna in 1920, keyed to the 1935 commune frame, from the curated research assembly regime-state 1935.xlsx, the author's compilation of official mid-1930s comuna statistics. The assembly carries no page-level citation, so the series documents a compilation rather than a direct extraction. Only 133 comunas carry a value; missing comunas are absent from the source, not zeros. A single-year cross-section.

inquilinaje.subtitle: Inquilinaje share, by comuna, 1935, proportion
inquilinaje.definition: Share of resident tenant labor (inquilinos) in the comuna, recorded as a proportion (values range 0 to 0.14), for 1935, from the curated research assembly regime-state 1935.xlsx, the author's compilation of official mid-1930s comuna statistics. The assembly carries no page-level citation, so the series documents a compilation rather than a direct extraction. Inquilinaje was the labor institution of the manorial estate system of the Central Valley. A single-year cross-section.

enf1920.subtitle: Enfranchised voters, by comuna, 1920, persons
enf1920.definition: Registered (enfranchised) voters in 1920, keyed to the 1935 commune frame, from the curated research assembly regime-state 1935.xlsx, the author's compilation of official mid-1930s comuna statistics. The assembly carries no page-level citation, so the series documents a compilation rather than a direct extraction drawn from the author's enfranchisement data collection 1862-1920. Comuna values sum to 328,034 nationally, matching the registered electorate of the 1920 election. A single-year cross-section.

enfrural.subtitle: Rural enfranchisement rate, by comuna, 1920, proportion
enfrural.definition: Rural enfranchisement in 1920 recorded as a small proportion (values below 0.005), keyed to the 1935 commune frame, from the curated research assembly regime-state 1935.xlsx, the author's compilation of official mid-1930s comuna statistics. The assembly carries no page-level citation, so the series documents a compilation rather than a direct extraction. The assembly does not document the denominator of the rate, so the base population is unresolved; use with caution.

bautismos.subtitle: Baptisms, by department, 1876–1880, baptisms
bautismos.definition: Baptisms registered by department, 1876-1880, from the vital-statistics cuadros of the Anuario Estadístico de la República de Chile entregas for those years (read from the Yumpu page images of the yearbook collection). Before the civil registry opened in 1885, parish baptisms are the working proxy for births. Column sums verified against printed or errata-corrected national totals.

nacimientos_1926.subtitle: Registered births, by department and province, 1926, births
nacimientos_1926.definition: Births registered by the civil registry in 1926, by department and province, from the Anuario Estadístico de Chile 1926, Vol. I (Demografía), Dirección General de Estadística. A single-year cross-section.

defunciones_1926.subtitle: Registered deaths, by department and province, 1926, deaths
defunciones_1926.definition: Deaths registered by the civil registry in 1926, by department and province, from the Anuario Estadístico de Chile 1926, Vol. I (Demografía), Dirección General de Estadística. A single-year cross-section.

matrimonios_1926.subtitle: Registered marriages, by department and province, 1926, marriages
matrimonios_1926.definition: Marriages registered by the civil registry in 1926, by department and province, from the Anuario Estadístico de Chile 1926, Vol. I (Demografía), Dirección General de Estadística. A single-year cross-section.

mortalidad_infantil_1926.subtitle: Infant deaths, by department and province, 1926, deaths under age one
mortalidad_infantil_1926.definition: Deaths of infants under one year of age registered in 1926, by department and province, from the Anuario Estadístico de Chile 1926, Vol. I (Demografía). A count of infant deaths, not a rate; divide by registered births (nacimientos_1926) for an infant mortality rate. A single-year cross-section.

defunciones_menores_1ano.subtitle: Deaths before the first birthday
defunciones_menores_1ano.definition: Deaths of children under one year of age, as returned by the civil register and compiled in the Anuario Estadístico. The series runs at department and province level from the early 1920s to 1948 and nationally back to 1851, which makes it one of the few welfare measures in the database with both a long national run and a subnational cross-section. It is a count, not a rate: to compare places, divide by live births in the same year rather than by population, because fertility differed sharply between the mining north and the agricultural centre.

mortinatos.subtitle: Stillbirths
mortinatos.definition: Stillbirths registered in the year. Chile counted these separately from infant deaths, so the series complements rather than duplicates deaths under one year. Coverage is national from 1900 and subnational from the 1920s. Registration of a stillbirth was less complete than of a live birth throughout the period, so levels are understated and the trend is more reliable than any single year.

poblacion_hombres.subtitle: Male population
poblacion_hombres.definition: Men enumerated at the census. Published here as one series across census years rather than as a separate variable per census, which is what the source tables look like. Sex ratios in 19th century Chile depart sharply from parity in the nitrate and coal districts, where male labour migration dominated, and in the rural centre, where it ran the other way.

poblacion_mujeres.subtitle: Female population
poblacion_mujeres.definition: Women enumerated at the census, the companion series to the male count. Reading the two together is the quickest way to see labour migration in the north and its absence in the agricultural core.

pop_censal.subtitle: Census population, Sinopsis retrospective
pop_censal.definition: Department population at each census from 1865 to 1920, as restated in the Sinopsis Estadística of 1924 to 1927. The Sinopsis recomputed earlier censuses onto the boundaries of its own day, so its figures can differ from the original census volumes for any department whose limits moved. Where both exist the database keeps them as separate indicators rather than choosing between them.

nacimientos_total.subtitle: Births, total
nacimientos_total.definition: Live births registered nationally, running from 1849 to 1925 in the Sinopsis retrospective tables. Civil registration began in 1885, so figures before that year come from parish registers and undercount by a margin that varied with the reach of the clergy.

defunciones_permil.subtitle: Deaths per 1,000 inhabitants
defunciones_permil.definition: The crude death rate by province in 1924, as printed in the Sinopsis. Crude rates confound mortality with age structure: a province with a young migrant population will show a low crude rate even where conditions are poor, which is exactly the situation in the nitrate provinces.

municipal_total_gastos.subtitle: Municipal expenditure, total
municipal_total_gastos.definition: Total spending by the municipality, from the Anuario tables that run across 1876 to 1892. This is the headline line of the municipal accounts and the denominator for the individual spending heads published alongside it. Values are nominal pesos and the peso depreciated substantially over the period, so compare shares between places in a year before comparing levels across years.

municipal_empleados_escritorio.subtitle: Clerical staff, municipal spending
municipal_empleados_escritorio.definition: Spending on the municipality's clerical establishment. Despite the name this is a peso amount and not a headcount, which the values settle: they carry centavos. Read against total expenditure it is the closest thing the 19th century accounts offer to a measure of local administrative capacity.

municipal_manutencion_presos.subtitle: Prisoner maintenance, municipal spending
municipal_manutencion_presos.definition: What the municipality spent feeding and housing prisoners. Chile placed this charge on the municipality rather than the treasury, so the line appears in local accounts and varies with whether the department seat held a gaol.

municipal_instruccion_publica.subtitle: Public instruction, municipal spending
municipal_instruccion_publica.definition: Municipal spending on schooling, distinct from the national education budget. It is often small or absent, which is itself the finding: primary instruction was overwhelmingly a central charge, and the municipal contribution marks the exceptions.

municipal_obras_publicas.subtitle: Public works, municipal spending
municipal_obras_publicas.definition: Municipal spending on public works. Lumpy by nature, since a single bridge or water scheme dominates a small municipality's year, so a spike is usually a project rather than a trend.

municipal_beneficencia.subtitle: Poor relief, municipal spending
municipal_beneficencia.definition: Municipal spending on charitable relief. Zero in most municipalities in most years, because relief in Chile ran through the Juntas de Beneficencia and the church rather than the town council; the non-zero entries mark where the council took it on directly.

fiscal_entradas_pesos.subtitle: Fiscal revenue
fiscal_entradas_pesos.definition: Total ordinary revenue of the Chilean treasury from 1833 to 1914, as compiled by Aldana in 1914 from the annual accounts. The series spans the shift from a customs based revenue system to one dominated by the nitrate export duty after 1880, which is the single largest structural break in Chilean public finance.

fiscal_gastos_pesos.subtitle: Fiscal expenditure
fiscal_gastos_pesos.definition: Total treasury expenditure from 1833 to 1914 on Aldana's compilation, the counterpart to ordinary revenue. Deficit years cluster around the War of the Pacific and the 1891 civil war.

renta_papel_sellado.subtitle: Stamped-paper duty revenue
renta_papel_sellado.definition: Revenue from the stamped paper required for legal instruments, 1838 to 1914. A small head in absolute terms but a useful one: it tracks the volume of formal legal and commercial transactions rather than trade, so it moves differently from customs.

renta_alcabala.subtitle: Alcabala revenue
renta_alcabala.definition: The colonial sales tax on property transfers, retained after independence and reported to 1890. Its slow decline is a fiscal history in miniature, as the republic shifted the burden onto trade.

aduana_entradas_pesos.subtitle: Customs receipts by port
aduana_entradas_pesos.definition: Duty collected at each customs house, 1831 to 1889, from the Memorias de Hacienda. This is the port level series that gives the database its clearest picture of where Chilean trade actually entered the country, and it shows Valparaíso's dominance giving way to the northern nitrate ports. Published on the map at port level, each port placed at the representative point of the modern comuna of the same name.

import_duty_rate_pct.subtitle: Import duty rate
import_duty_rate_pct.definition: Duties collected as a percentage of the value of imports, an effective rather than a statutory rate. It falls when high value low duty goods dominate the import bill, so it is a measure of the composition of trade as much as of tariff policy.

profesion_agricultores_total.subtitle: Farmers
profesion_agricultores_total.definition: Persons returning agricultor as their occupation at the 1875 census. The census distinguished agricultores from labradores, and the two coexist in the same departments rather than substituting for one another, so they record different positions in the rural hierarchy rather than two words for the same job. Read the two together before drawing conclusions about the agrarian structure.

profesion_jornaleros_total.subtitle: Day labourers
profesion_jornaleros_total.definition: Persons returning jornalero at the 1875 census, the largest single occupational category in most departments and the closest thing the census offers to a count of unattached wage labour.

profesion_sirvientes_total.subtitle: Servants
profesion_sirvientes_total.definition: Domestic servants at the 1875 census. Overwhelmingly women, and concentrated in the cities and the large estates, which makes it a useful proxy for household wealth where no wealth measure exists.

profesion_medicos_i_cirujanos_total.subtitle: Physicians and surgeons
profesion_medicos_i_cirujanos_total.definition: Medical practitioners at the 1875 census. The printed census used two different row labels for this occupation in different departments, Médicos in some and Médicos i cirujanos in others, so the two were extracted as separate variables and each covered only part of the country. They are merged here into one indicator; the merge is lossless because the two never both report for the same department.

profesion_profesores_i_preceptores_total.subtitle: Teachers and preceptors
profesion_profesores_i_preceptores_total.definition: Teaching staff at the 1875 census, merged from the two row labels the printed census used in different departments on the same basis as the medical count.

profesion_cat_agricultura_total.subtitle: Occupied in agriculture
profesion_cat_agricultura_total.definition: Persons in the agricultural category of the 1920 census occupational classification. The 1920 categories are broad groupings rather than the individual trades of 1875, so the two censuses are not directly comparable at this level of detail.

existencias_bovinos_cabezas.subtitle: Cattle
existencias_bovinos_cabezas.definition: Head of cattle returned by the agricultural statistics. Livestock counts of this period rest on declarations by owners with a tax interest in the answer, so treat levels as a floor and pay more attention to the geography than to the totals.

existencias_ovinos_cabezas.subtitle: Sheep
existencias_ovinos_cabezas.definition: Head of sheep. The far southern provinces dominate from the late 19th century as the Magallanes sheep economy develops, and that concentration is the main signal in the series.

trigo_rendimiento_qqha.subtitle: Wheat yield
trigo_rendimiento_qqha.definition: Wheat yield in metric quintals per hectare from the ODEPA agricultural statistics, 1965 to 1974. Yield is the ratio of two separately reported series, so a province with a small sown area can produce an implausible figure from a rounding error in either.

cultivos_sementeras_total_ha.subtitle: Sown crops, area
cultivos_sementeras_total_ha.definition: Total area under sown crops by province in 1924 and 1925, from the Sinopsis. The companion pasture and tree crop series use the same classification, so the three sum to the cultivated area.

liceos_hombres_matricula.subtitle: Liceo enrolment, boys
liceos_hombres_matricula.definition: Boys enrolled in the state secondary liceos, by city, 1900 to 1909. The liceo network was small, deliberately selective and concentrated in provincial capitals, so this measures the reach of secondary schooling rather than its scale.

liceos_ninas_matricula.subtitle: Liceo enrolment, girls
liceos_ninas_matricula.definition: Girls enrolled in the state secondary liceos. Girls' liceos were founded later and in fewer cities than boys', and the gap between the two series is the clearest measure in the database of how unevenly secondary schooling opened to women.

escuelas_primarias_matricula_total.subtitle: Primary school enrolment
escuelas_primarias_matricula_total.definition: Children enrolled in primary schools by department in 1909, from the Anuario. Enrolment is not attendance: the companion average attendance series runs well below it, and the ratio of the two is the more informative measure.

matricula_total_hombres.subtitle: School enrolment, male
matricula_total_hombres.definition: Boys enrolled in schools by province in 1900, from the Sinopsis. Reported alongside the female count and the separate returns for boys', girls' and mixed schools.

correos_cartas.subtitle: Letters posted
correos_cartas.definition: Letters posted by department, drawn from the Memorias del Interior for 1876, 1877, 1878, 1881 and 1882. The source stores each year as its own variable; they are published here as one series, which is why a chart shows five cross-sections rather than an annual run. Postal traffic per head is one of the better available proxies for literacy and commercial activity before the census began measuring either.

correos_impresos.subtitle: Printed matter posted
correos_impresos.definition: Newspapers, circulars and other printed matter posted by department across seven years between 1876 and 1886. It moves with the reach of the press rather than with private correspondence, so it complements the letter series.

telegrafo_oficina_empleados.subtitle: Telegraph office staff
telegrafo_oficina_empleados.definition: Staff employed at each telegraph office in 1891 and 1892, from the Memoria del Interior. With the companion count of instruments it maps the state's communications network at city level in the years around the civil war.

inscriptos.subtitle: Registered electors
inscriptos.definition: Men on the electoral register by department, 1915 to 1921. Registration in this period was a contested and locally administered process, so the series measures the outcome of that contest as much as it measures the eligible population.

votos_municipales_1870.subtitle: Votes cast, municipal election of 1870
votos_municipales_1870.definition: Votes recorded in the 1870 municipal elections by department, from the electoral census printed in the Anuario of 1871. Read against the count of calificados in the same table to get turnout among those qualified to vote.

has_gobernador_interior.subtitle: Department has a resident governor
has_gobernador_interior.definition: Whether the Memoria del Interior records a governor in residence in the department, 1867 to 1876. A crude but direct indicator of where the central state was physically present, and one of the few such measures available for the period.

vacunados_total.subtitle: Persons vaccinated
vacunados_total.definition: Smallpox vaccinations performed, by department, in 1862, 1886 and 1889. The three years are the ones the Memorias del Interior reported at department level, and each follows an epidemic, so the series records the response to outbreaks rather than routine coverage.

junta_vacuna_ingresos_total.subtitle: Vaccination board revenue
junta_vacuna_ingresos_total.definition: Income of the departmental Junta de Vacuna, 1889 to 1892. The boards were funded partly by a fiscal allocation and partly locally, and the split between the two is reported separately.

viruela_defunciones.subtitle: Smallpox deaths
viruela_defunciones.definition: Deaths from smallpox by department, 1886 to 1894, spanning the severe epidemic of the early 1890s. Read with the vaccination series, which responds to it.

viviendas_total_1992.subtitle: Dwellings, total (1992)
viviendas_total_1992.definition: Total dwellings enumerated by the 1992 census at commune level, the denominator for the water, sewerage, lighting and tenure series published alongside it.

pct_gasto_guerra.subtitle: War ministry share of fiscal spending, 1842–1900, %
pct_gasto_guerra.definition: Expenditure by the Ministerio de Guerra as a percentage of total fiscal spending, at thirteen benchmark years from 1842 to 1900. This is the largest single head in the early series and the one that moves most: it opens at 35.2% in 1842, when the army still absorbed more than a third of the budget, and falls steadily as instruction, public works and colonisation claim shares of their own. Read it together with the Navy and Treasury heads rather than alone, since the eleven ministry shares are a closed decomposition and sum to 100% in ten of the thirteen years; the remaining three miss by between 0.02 and 3.0 points, which is printed rounding and a small head the source omits, not a gap in the data.

pct_gasto_marina.subtitle: Navy ministry share of fiscal spending, 1842–1900, %
pct_gasto_marina.definition: Expenditure by the Ministerio de Marina as a percentage of total fiscal spending, at thirteen benchmark years from 1842 to 1900. The naval share is the one place in the budget where the War of the Pacific is legible: Chile fought it at sea first, and the series carries the build-up and the subsequent settling. The Navy is reported separately from War throughout, so the two must be added to recover total military spending; neither is a complete measure of it on its own.

pct_gasto_hacienda.subtitle: Treasury ministry share of fiscal spending, 1842–1900, %
pct_gasto_hacienda.definition: Expenditure by the Ministerio de Hacienda as a percentage of total fiscal spending, at thirteen benchmark years from 1842 to 1900. The head is larger than a finance ministry would suggest to a modern reader, 42.2% in 1842, because it carries debt service and the customs administration alongside the ministry's own costs. It is therefore a poor proxy for bureaucratic size and a good one for the weight of borrowing and of the customs house in nineteenth-century Chilean public finance.

pct_participacion.subtitle: Turnout as % of the electoral register, 1935, by province
pct_participacion.definition: Votes cast as a percentage of registered voters, by province, 1935. The denominator is the REGISTER, not the adult population, which is why the figures sit between 69% and 92% and must not be read as participation rates in the modern sense: registration was itself restricted and the unregistered never enter the calculation. The published percentage reproduces votantes_total divided by inscritos_total for seventeen of the nineteen provinces within a tenth of a point, so it is the source's own arithmetic on the two columns beside it rather than an independent measurement.

inscritos_total.subtitle: Registered voters, general and municipal rolls, 1935
inscritos_total.definition: Total registered voters by province, 1935, the sum of the general and municipal rolls reported separately alongside it. Chile kept two registers with different franchises, so the total is the right denominator for national turnout while the two components are what distinguish the congressional from the municipal electorate. Registration, not population, is the boundary of the political nation in this table.

reos_por_1000_hab.subtitle: Prison admissions per 1,000 inhabitants, 1935
reos_por_1000_hab.definition: Prison admissions per thousand inhabitants by province, 1935. The denominator is the official 1935 population estimate printed in the same cuadro and published here as poblacion_calculada_1935, not a census count, so the rate inherits whatever error that estimate carries in the fast-growing nitrate provinces. It measures admissions rather than the standing prison population, so a province with short sentences and high throughput scores above one with fewer, longer ones.

pct_ebriedad.subtitle: Drunkenness as % of all arrests, 1935, by province
pct_ebriedad.definition: Arrests for drunkenness as a percentage of all arrests, by province, 1935. The share reproduces the two adjacent columns for eighteen of nineteen provinces, so it is the source's own ratio. What it measures is policing as much as drinking: an ebriedad arrest required an officer to make one, so the indicator moves with the density of the police as well as with consumption, and it is best read against the total arrest count rather than on its own.

total_km.subtitle: Road network, total kilometres, 1935, by province
total_km.definition: Total length of the provincial road network in kilometres, 1935. It is exactly the sum of the two components published beside it, roads carrying motor and cart traffic and pack trails, for all sixteen provinces that report both, so the total conceals a distinction worth keeping: a province whose kilometres are mostly troperos had length without wheeled access. Read the components before the total.

vacunos_consumo_kg_per_hab.subtitle: Beef per inhabitant, kilograms, 1935, by province
vacunos_consumo_kg_per_hab.definition: Kilograms of beef per inhabitant by province, 1935. It does NOT reconcile to the beef tonnage divided by the provincial population printed in the same table, agreeing for only twelve of nineteen provinces, so the source is using a different base or accounting for meat moved between provinces. Slaughter is recorded where the animal was killed, not where the meat was eaten, which makes this a measure of provincial slaughter capacity as much as of provincial diet.

valor_total_pesos.subtitle: Value of mining production, pesos, 1935, by province
valor_total_pesos.definition: Total value of mining production in current pesos by province, 1935. The distribution is the point: the median province produces about four million pesos and the largest produces 568 million, so a linear scale renders the country as one province and a blank map. This is the nitrate and copper north as a share of the national economy, stated in money rather than tonnage, and the peso figure is nominal and not comparable across years.

giros_emitidos_valor.subtitle: Postal money orders issued, value in pesos, 1935
giros_emitidos_valor.definition: Value of postal money orders issued in a province, 1935, reported alongside the value paid. The pair is a rare direct trace of internal remittance: a province that issues far more than it pays is sending money out, typically the mining north paying wages home, and one that pays more than it issues is receiving it. Neither column alone shows the flow.

automoviles_particulares.subtitle: Private motor cars registered, 1935, by province
automoviles_particulares.definition: Motor cars registered for private use by province, 1935, reported separately from cars for hire. The split matters more than the total in a country this unequal: private registration tracks provincial wealth, while cars for hire track the presence of a market for movement and appear in provinces with little private ownership. Registration is not the vehicle stock, since it captures only what was declared.

ingreso_real_promedio_total.subtitle: Average annual real earnings, all sectors, 1940–1952
ingreso_real_promedio_total.definition: Average annual real earnings across all sectors, in pesos of 1961, 1940 to 1952, from Mamalakis's Historical Statistics of Chile. Earnings and the salary series published beside it are drawn from two different tables and are not the same quantity: in finance and manufacturing the average salary exceeds the average earning, which is only possible if the two populations differ, so do not read the sector salary as a component of the sector earning. Both are deflated to 1961 and neither is comparable to a nominal peso figure elsewhere in the atlas.

salario_real_promedio_all_industries_per.subtitle: Average annual real salary per employee, 1940–1952
salario_real_promedio_all_industries_per.definition: Average annual real salary per employee across all industries, in pesos of 1961, 1940 to 1952, from Mamalakis's Historical Statistics of Chile. The per-employee denominator is what separates this from the earnings series: it divides by employment rather than by the whole earning population, so sectors with many low-paid non-employees do not drag it down. Use the sector series rather than this aggregate when the composition of employment is itself changing, which across these twelve years it is.

matrimonios_20-24.subtitle: Marriages, age group 20 to 24, 1964–1973
matrimonios_20-24.definition: Marriages recorded in the 20 to 24 age band, 1964 to 1973, from Mamalakis's Historical Statistics of Chile. The source cuadro is headed simply Matrimonios por grupo de edad and does NOT state whose age indexes the table; the strong skew toward the younger bands is consistent with the bride's age but the atlas does not assert it, and any use that depends on which spouse is being counted needs the printed volume. The fourteen bands are a complete partition, so they sum to total marriages for the year.

liceos_hombres_asistencia.subtitle: Boys' liceo average attendance, 1900–1909, by town
liceos_hombres_asistencia.definition: Average daily attendance at the boys' liceo of each town, 1900 to 1909, from the Anuario Estadístico de Chile 1909. Read it against the matrícula series rather than alone: enrolment measures how many families put a son on the roll and attendance measures how many actually came, and the gap between them, roughly a quarter at the median, is the more informative quantity. The unit is the establishment, so a town with two liceos is not comparable to one with a single larger school.

population_urban.subtitle: Urban population of Chilean towns, 1875–1930
population_urban.definition: Population of the urban centre itself at the census years 1875 to 1930, taken from the census volumes rather than reconstructed. The unit is the town and not its department, so these figures are much smaller than the department populations elsewhere in the atlas and the two must never be mixed in one series. Boundaries of what counted as urban were redrawn between censuses, so a jump can record a definitional change rather than growth.

telegrafos_oficina_empleados_count.subtitle: Telegraph office staff, 1889, by office
telegrafos_oficina_empleados_count.definition: Number of employees at each telegraph office in the national nómina of 1889, from the Memoria del Interior. The median office has one employee and the largest has thirteen, which is the shape of the thing: the network was a thin filament of one-person offices anchored on a few hubs. Because the unit is the office and not the town, this is a direct measure of state presence at a place, one of the few available for the 1880s at this grain.

colera_ausilio_municipal_pesos.subtitle: Municipal cholera relief spending, pesos, 1886–1887
colera_ausilio_municipal_pesos.definition: Pesos of municipal relief spending during the cholera epidemic of 1886 to 1887, by town. This is emergency expenditure and not a budget line, so it measures where the epidemic struck and where a municipality had the money to respond, two things the number cannot separate. A zero is not evidence that cholera spared a town.

municipal_presupuesto_pesos.subtitle: Municipal budget, pesos, 1895, by comuna
municipal_presupuesto_pesos.definition: Budgeted municipal revenue in pesos for 1895, by comuna, from the Memoria del Interior. This is the first year of the atlas at comuna grain: the Ley de Comuna Autónoma of 1891 created the units and this cuadro is an early census of what they could actually raise. The spread is the finding, from a median of about 25,000 pesos to Santiago's 3.4 million, and it is a budget figure rather than a realised account.

cabotaje_extracciones_pesos.subtitle: Coastal shipments out of port, pesos, 1852–1858
cabotaje_extracciones_pesos.definition: Value in pesos of goods shipped OUT of each port in the coastal trade, 1852 to 1858, reported against the introducciones shipped in. Cabotaje is domestic trade between Chilean ports and is a different account from the customs series: it measures internal circulation rather than foreign commerce, and it is the best pre-railway evidence of which regions the national market actually reached.

rainfall_mm_santiago.subtitle: Rainfall, Santiago, 1866–1909, millimetres a year
rainfall_mm_santiago.definition: Annual rainfall at Santiago in millimetres, 1866 to 1909, from the retrospective cuadro in the Anuario Estadístico de 1909. Forty-four consecutive years make this one of the longest unbroken annual series in the atlas, and its interest is the variance rather than the mean: the driest year, 1892 at 124 mm, delivered a sixth of the wettest, 1900 at 820 mm, on a central valley whose agriculture was rain-fed above the irrigation canals. One station is one station, and the figure describes Santiago rather than Chile.

rainfall_days_count_santiago.subtitle: Days of rain, Santiago, 1866–1909, days a year
rainfall_days_count_santiago.definition: Number of days on which rain was recorded at Santiago, 1866 to 1909, from the same Anuario 1909 cuadro as the millimetre series. It is worth reading beside the depth rather than instead of it: the two move together but not tightly, correlating at 0.82, and the median year concentrates its rain into about 7 mm per rainy day, so a year can be wet in days and dry in water. Days of rain range from 21 to 88.

hospital_sb_mujeres_entrados.subtitle: Admissions, Hospital San Francisco de Borja, Santiago, 1840–1858
hospital_sb_mujeres_entrados.definition: Women admitted each year to the Hospital San Francisco de Borja, Santiago's general hospital for women, 1840 to 1858, from the Anuario Estadístico 1860-72. Admissions run from 3,097 to 5,924 and roughly double over the nineteen years, faster than the city grew, so this measures the hospital's reach as much as the incidence of illness. Read with the men's hospital, San Juan de Dios, which admitted about twice as many.

hospital_sb_mujeres_salidos.subtitle: Discharges, Hospital San Francisco de Borja, Santiago, 1840–1858
hospital_sb_mujeres_salidos.definition: Women discharged alive each year from the Hospital San Francisco de Borja, 1840 to 1858. Discharges plus deaths do not equal admissions in any of the nineteen years, differing by between −72 and +126: the residual is the stock of patients carried across 31 December, which the source cuadro does not print. Treat the three columns as a movement account with an unstated opening and closing balance rather than a closed identity.

hospital_sb_mujeres_muertos.subtitle: Deaths, Hospital San Francisco de Borja, Santiago, 1840–1858
hospital_sb_mujeres_muertos.definition: Women who died in the Hospital San Francisco de Borja, 1840 to 1858. Against admissions this is a hospital mortality rate of 17 to 33 per hundred, median 19, well above the men's hospital across the same years, and the gap should not be read as a difference in the illnesses so much as in who reached the wards: a nineteenth-century general hospital admitted the destitute sick, and the two institutions drew on different populations. The Anuario prints the same nineteen values a second time, under a per-establishment cuadro that also decomposes them by age band.

hospital_sjd_hombres_entrados.subtitle: Admissions, Hospital San Juan de Dios, Santiago, 1840–1858
hospital_sjd_hombres_entrados.definition: Men admitted each year to the Hospital San Juan de Dios, Santiago's general hospital for men, 1840 to 1858, from the Anuario Estadístico 1860-72. Admissions run from 5,933 to 9,533, roughly twice the women's hospital in every year of the run. This is the older and larger of the two Santiago foundations and the series is the closest thing the database holds to a continuous pre-1860 measure of urban hospital use.

hospital_sjd_hombres_salidos.subtitle: Discharges, Hospital San Juan de Dios, Santiago, 1840–1858
hospital_sjd_hombres_salidos.definition: Men discharged alive each year from the Hospital San Juan de Dios, 1840 to 1858. As at San Borja, discharges plus deaths do not close against admissions in any year, here by between −316 and +233, because the cuadro prints no opening or closing patient stock. The residual is small against admissions of six to nine thousand and is the carry-over across the year end, not an extraction error.
